The story is tightly unified around the central metaphor and plot of the building's missing waterproofing membrane. It follows a clear, logical progression: the beginning establishes the discovery of the mold and the fifty-four-year-old structural flaw; the middle details the disruptive, slow-moving repair process and how the physical decay of the building mirrors the fracturing and attrition within the academic department; and the end provides a quiet, satisfying resolution when Helen finally sees and touches the newly installed membrane. Every character detail, piece of dialogue, and metaphor (such as comparing institutional movement to rain seeping through concrete, or departmental divisions to hairline cracks) serves the overarching themes of endurance, institutional neglect, and the passage of time, creating a harmonious and deeply engaging whole.
